entities.name: Sri Vijaya Rajasinha of Kandy
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Sri Vijaya Rajasinha, who reigned as King of Kandy from 1739 to 1747, marked a pivotal period in the Kandyan kingdom's history, solidifying the influence of the Madurai Nayak dynasty on the Sinhala throne and initiating a significant cultural and religious revival. Born into the Telugu-speaking Madurai Nayak family, he was the brother of Queen Pramila, consort to his predecessor Vira Narendra Sinha. His ascension, facilitated by his prior residence in Kandy and familiarity with its political landscape and Buddhist traditions, represented a deliberate strategy to secure the royal line through a matrilineal connection to the previous monarch, thus preserving a semblance of continuity despite the foreign lineage.

During his eight-year reign, Vijaya Rajasinha faced the persistent challenge of Dutch colonial power, which controlled the lucrative coastal regions of Ceylon and sought to restrict Kandyan access to the outside world. He engaged in diplomatic efforts, including an unsuccessful embassy to Siam in 1740, aimed at securing Buddhist monks to re-establish the upasampada (higher ordination) which had lapsed in Sri Lanka, a critical religious objective. Internally, he championed the revival of Buddhism, fostering closer ties with the Sangha and promoting temple restoration. His rule also saw increased integration of Nayak cultural practices within the Kandyan court, influencing art, architecture, and courtly rituals, while simultaneously respecting and supporting the Sinhala Buddhist identity.
